summary: Saint-Georges-de-l'Oyapock Airport serves the easternmost commune of French Guiana, situated along the Oyapock River which forms the border with Brazil. The airport provides an important air link to Cayenne and serves as a key access point for travelers heading to the Brazilian border town of Oiapoque via the nearby Oyapock River Bridge. As French Guiana is an overseas department of France, the airport also functions as a European Union border entry point in the Amazon region.
faqs:
Q: How do you get from the airport to Oiapoque, Brazil?
A: The airport is approximately 3 km from the Oyapock River Bridge, which connects French Guiana to Brazil. Taxis are available at the airport to take you to the border crossing, where you can walk across to Oiapoque.

Q: Are there regular flights to Cayenne?
A: Yes, the airport is primarily served by regional flights connecting Saint-Georges to Cayenne-Félix Eboué Airport, with limited scheduled service.

Q: Do I need a visa to cross into Brazil from this airport?
A: Visa requirements depend on your nationality. Brazilian and EU citizens generally have different requirements, and you should check current entry regulations before traveling.

Q: Is the airport open at night?
A: The airport has limited operating hours and primarily handles daytime flights. Confirm your flight schedule in advance as night operations are not available.
transport_tips: Taxis are the main ground transport option from the airport and can take you into Saint-Georges town or directly to the Oyapock River Bridge for the crossing into Brazil. There is no public bus service connecting the airport to nearby destinations, so arranging transport in advance is recommended. The small terminal means ground services are informal, so have local currency (euros) ready for fares.
local_tip: If you're crossing into Brazil, take a photo of the Oyapock River Bridge from the French side at sunset, it is one of the most iconic border landmarks in South America and rarely crowded.
